# Validate tool input against the registered inputSchema

Issue: re-cinq/HALEngine#37
Labels: priority:medium, type:feature, size:M, area:tools, epic:extension-points

Part of #35

## Why

`ToolRegistry.execute` looks a tool up, logs the input's key names, and calls the executor
without ever checking the declared `inputSchema` (`src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts`).
Every tool declares a JSON Schema (`src/types/ai.ts`) that is handed verbatim to both
providers, but nothing validates what comes back from the model. The shipped example shows the
shape of the problem: `example/weather-tool.ts` declares `location` as a required string, then
casts and defaults it (`(input.location as string) || 'Unknown'`) with a comment warning the reader
that `inputSchema` shapes what the model sends but does not enforce it. That is the careful version,
written by the people who wrote the engine — and it still answers a malformed call with a
confidently formatted forecast for `'Unknown'` rather than telling the model it got the call wrong.

The registry currently pushes this check onto each tool's own executor, leaving every consumer
to implement it itself — differently each time, or not at all. A tool that receives unexpected input must fail
in one predictable, known way before the rest of this epic's tool work can be built on top
of it.

## What to do

Validate `input` against the resolved tool definition's `inputSchema` inside
`ToolRegistry.execute`, before the executor runs, using a JSON Schema validator (`ajv`
unless the build proves otherwise) added to `dependencies` — not a second, hand-written
schema in a different format, since the schema already has to match what is handed to the
providers.

Compile a static tool's schema once at `register` time so a broken schema fails at startup,
not mid-conversation; a schema produced by a function-valued `ToolDefinitionSource`
resolves and compiles per call, cached by the resolved schema object.

A rejection returns a `ToolResponse` (`{result: '<what was wrong>'}`) rather than throwing,
so a malformed call becomes something the model can read and correct within the existing
`DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS = 5` budget, instead of ending the whole conversation with a
generic transport error. Validation enforces `required`, declared types and `enum` only —
it does not inject `additionalProperties: false`, coerce types, or apply defaults, and
there is no opt-out flag.

Update `docs/adding-a-tool.md`, `README.md` and `.specify/spec.md` to match.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ToolRegistry.execute` validates `input` against the resolved definition's
      `inputSchema` before calling the executor; on failure it returns a `ToolResponse`
      whose `result` describes the failure, and the executor is never invoked
- [ ] A new `src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts` (the registry has no test file today)
      registers a tool requiring a `location` string, calls `execute` with `{}`, and
      asserts the returned result names `location` as required and the executor's call
      count is `0`
- [ ] A test asserts valid input with an unlisted extra property is passed through to the
      executor unchanged (`toEqual`, so an added default or coerced value fails the test) —
      exactly once
- [ ] A test asserts a wrong-typed field (a number where a string is required) is rejected
      with a message naming the field path and the expected type, and that the message does
      **not** contain the offending value
- [ ] A test asserts `register` throws at registration time for an uncompilable schema, and
      that the thrown message names the tool
- [ ] A test asserts a function-valued tool definition whose returned schema differs between
      calls is validated against the schema current at that call, not a stale cached one
- [ ] A test asserts a static tool's schema is compiled once across ten `execute` calls
- [ ] A tool-loop test in `chatOrchestrator.test.ts` drives a stub provider through a
      rejected tool call followed by a corrected retry, and asserts `processMessage`
      resolves — not rejects — with the rejection text visible to the provider on the next
      round
- [ ] `execute` still throws `Unknown tool: <name>` for an unregistered name, unchanged,
      pinned by a test
- [ ] Rejection messages and log lines name the failing property paths and the constraint
      that failed, and never a property **value**. Tool input is where identifying data
      enters the engine and the engine redacts nothing today. A test asserts a rejected
      payload containing an identifying field produces no log line and no returned text
      containing that field's value
- [ ] `execute` carries a **one-line** doc comment — `re-lint/max-comment-lines` rejects a
      `@param`/`@returns`/`@throws` block — and the full contract (rejection `ToolResponse` for input
      the schema rejects, throw only for an unknown tool name) is stated in
      `specs/hal-engine-tool-input-validation/spec.md`, which the comment points at
- [ ] The validator is in `package.json` `dependencies`, not `peerDependencies` or
      `devDependencies`, and
      `npm run build && node --input-type=module -e "import('./dist/index.js')"` exits `0`
- [ ] `README.md` states what the registry now does, and the claim is true rather than
      merely present
- [ ] `docs/adding-a-tool.md` no longer tells executors to cast defensively and handle
      missing input; it states that input reaching an executor has already passed the
      declared schema, that unknown keys may still be present, and that a rejection is
      returned to the model rather than thrown
- [ ] `.specify/spec.md` records that a rejection is a tool result (not an exception), that
      the tool-round bound is what stops a retry cycle from spinning, and that extra
      properties pass through unmodified
- [ ] The PR body states the migration note: an executor that used to hand-validate its
      input now receives only input the schema already accepts, and a tool that relied on
      seeing malformed input to produce its own error message stops seeing it. The version
      bump is MINOR
- [ ] Every test this issue adds cites the statement it validates with an inline
      `([validated by ...])` link in a `specs/**` or `adrs/**` file, and the statements exist
      before the tests do. `re-lint/require-spec-link` fails the build on an uncited test, so the
      spec edits are part of this issue rather than a follow-up
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` carries an entry for this change, written for somebody reading it on npm
      rather than somebody reading this repo's log. CI runs `scripts/check-changelog.sh` and
      fails any PR touching a non-test file under `src/` without one
- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run eslint` (`--max-warnings 0`)
      and `npm run prettier:check` pass, with no `any` in the changed public surface

## Tech notes

Today's `throw` in `registry.ts` propagates through the orchestrator's tool-call
`Promise.all`, out of the processing loop's `try`, fires `onError`, and reaches the
WebSocket error handler, which sends a generic "Failed to process message" and never sends
the stream-end frame. That end-to-end path is why a rejection has to be a returned
`ToolResponse` instead of a throw.

Deliberately out of scope: the `Unknown tool: <name>` throw stays as-is — the same failure
class handled the opposite way, which is an intentional split, but changing it affects
direct callers and is tracked as *Return an unknown tool name to the model instead of
throwing*. Also out of scope: validating tool *output*; hallucination detection and an
evaluation harness; per-tool authorization — a schema-valid call for someone else's data is still
valid, and authorization is a separate `ToolContext` boundary concern that no issue in this epic
owns (*Let a consumer decline a tool call through a `beforeToolCall` hook* is a veto seam, not an
authorization model); retry, timeout
and rate limiting around tool execution; and any actual tool implementation, which is
written against this contract later.

# Definition of Done

> `ToolRegistry.execute` looks a tool up, logs the input's key names, and calls the executor
> without ever checking the declared `inputSchema` (`src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts`).
> Every tool declares a JSON Schema (`src/types/ai.ts`) that is handed verbatim to both
> providers, but nothing validates what comes back from the model.

**Strategy: `direct`** — `ToolRegistry.register`, `ToolRegistry.execute` and `createChatOrchestrator` already expose the exact entry points this ticket changes, so the acceptance tests call them directly today and fail because schema compilation and input validation are absent.

## Done when these pass

- [ ] **rejects input missing a required property with a ToolResponse and never calls the executor** — `ToolRegistry.execute` validates `input` against `inputSchema`, returns a `ToolResponse` naming the missing required property, and does not invoke the executor.
      `src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts`

- [ ] **rejects a wrong-typed property naming the field and expected type without leaking the offending value to the result or logs** — `ToolRegistry.execute` rejects a property with the wrong JSON Schema type without calling the executor, names the failing field path and expected type in `result`, and omits the offending property value from both `result` and emitted log lines.
      `src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts`

- [ ] **throws at register time naming the tool when a static inputSchema cannot be compiled** — `ToolRegistry.register` compiles a static `ToolDefinition`'s `inputSchema` once at registration time and throws synchronously naming the tool when the schema is invalid.
      `src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts`

- [ ] **returns a schema rejection as a tool_result in the orchestrator loop so the model can correct the call on the next round** — `createChatOrchestrator` feeds a schema-rejected tool call's `ToolResponse.result` back to the provider as a `tool_result` without invoking the executor on the invalid call, allowing the model to retry with valid arguments and complete the turn.
      `src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts`

## Facets

- [x] Add `ajv` to `dependencies` in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` (`strict: false`, `validateFormats: false`, no coercion, no defaults, no injected `additionalProperties: false`) and bump the package version `MINOR`.
- [x] Compile static `ToolDefinition.inputSchema` at `ToolRegistry.register` time (throwing an error naming the tool on invalid schemas).
- [x] Cache compiled validators for function-valued `ToolDefinitionSource` schemas by schema object reference (`WeakMap`).
- [x] Validate `input` in `ToolRegistry.execute` before invoking the executor, returning a `ToolResponse` (`{result}`) that names failing field paths and expected types/required fields without echoing or logging offending values, and add the one-line doc comment pointing at `specs/hal-engine-tool-input-validation/spec.md`.
- [x] Name the enum constraint in a rejection without echoing the rejected value, and normalize required-field messages.
- [x] Normalize nested `dataPath` validator errors to field paths so rejection text and logs name the field.
- [x] Normalize bracket-quoted legacy `missingProperty` errors before formatting required-field paths, and repair the registry test's member chains reported by CI.
- [x] Repair the five CI lint findings in `registry.test.ts` and derive type rejection text from constraint metadata so validator messages cannot echo input values.
- [x] Repair the latest CI type and lint findings, and log the failing field path with its expected type without logging the rejected value.
- [x] Repair four CI `max-expects` findings and preserve a bracket-quoted legacy field name containing `]` in rejection paths.
- [x] Repair the seven CI lint findings in `registry.test.ts` and preserve a schema-valid empty location in the worked weather tool with a focused test and spec link.
- [x] Repair the latest CI type and lint findings and pin a static tool's single schema compilation across ten executions.
- [x] Repair the CI helper-order lint finding and pin schema-valid extra-property pass-through in `src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts` with its spec link.
- [ ] Add the remaining unit tests in `src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts` and `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts`, link their statements in `specs/hal-engine-tool-input-validation/spec.md`, and complete the tool documentation updates.

## Out of scope

- Output validation and domain sanity checks (covered by ADR-002), MCP tool-server discovery and proxying (#42), per-tool authorization or `beforeToolCall` hooks (#40), retry/timeout/rate-limiting around tool execution, and concrete tool implementations.

# Tool Input Validation

| Field  | Value                |
| ------ | -------------------- |
| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#37 |
| Status | In Progress          |

Every tool registered in `src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts` declares a JSON Schema `inputSchema` that is forwarded to the configured AI provider, and `ToolRegistry.execute` validates the model-supplied `input` against that schema before calling the tool's executor. When validation fails, `execute` returns a rejection `ToolResponse` describing what was wrong rather than throwing, so the orchestrator feeds the failure back to the model as a `tool_result` within the existing tool-round budget.

## Validation at execute time

- When `input` omits a property listed in `required`, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` whose `result` names the missing property as required and never invokes the executor. Its field path escapes JSON Pointer characters such as `/`, including when a validator reports the missing name in bracket notation ([validated by: rejects input missing a required property with a ToolResponse and never calls the executor](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L16); [validated by: escapes a required field name in the rejection path without invoking the executor](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L172); [validated by: normalizes a legacy required-property error with a slash](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L184)).
- When `input` supplies a property whose value does not match its declared JSON Schema type, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` naming the failing field path and expected type without invoking the executor, and neither `result` nor the emitted log record contains the offending property value. This also applies to a validator error with a nested `dataPath` or a message containing the value ([validated by: rejects a wrong-typed property naming the field and expected type without leaking the offending value to the result or logs](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L46); [validated by: names a nested wrong-typed field from a dataPath error without echoing its value](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L247); [validated by: does not echo a validator message containing the rejected property value](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L228)).
- A type rejection log record names the failing field path and expected type, without recording the rejected value ([validated by: logs the expected type and field path for a rejected tool input](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L119)).
- A legacy validator's bracket-quoted field name containing `]` remains one escaped field-path segment in a type rejection ([validated by: keeps a bracket-quoted field containing a closing bracket in the rejection path](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L209)).
- When `input` satisfies `required`, declared property types and `enum`, `ToolRegistry.execute` invokes the executor once and passes the input object through unchanged — including undeclared extra properties — without injecting `additionalProperties: false`, coercing types or applying defaults ([validated by: passes schema-valid input with an extra property to the executor unchanged once](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L272)). An enum rejection names its field path and the enum constraint without repeating the rejected value ([validated by: names the enum constraint without exposing the rejected value](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L146)).
- When `ToolRegistry.execute` is called with a tool name that has not been registered, it throws `Unknown tool: <name>` because an unregistered tool is a programming or configuration error rather than a recoverable input mistake.

## Schema compilation and caching

- A static `ToolDefinition` has its `inputSchema` compiled once at `register` time, so a schema that is not valid JSON Schema throws synchronously from `register` with an error message naming the offending tool ([validated by: throws at register time naming the tool when a static inputSchema cannot be compiled](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L94)).
- Registration of a static tool with an invalid JSON Schema type throws immediately and names that tool ([validated by: rejects an invalid static input schema while registering the named tool](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L48)).
- A static tool's `inputSchema` is compiled at `register` time and reused on every `execute` call without re-reading or re-compiling `definition.inputSchema` ([validated by: compiles a static tool schema once across ten executions](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L64)).
- A function-valued `ToolDefinitionSource` resolves its definition on each `execute` call and validates against the `inputSchema` returned for that call, caching compiled validators by schema object reference (`WeakMap`) so distinct returned schemas each enforce their own rules ([validated by: compiles each dynamic schema object once and validates against the current one](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L89)).

## Orchestrator tool-loop recovery

- Because a schema rejection returns a `ToolResponse` instead of throwing, `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` sends the rejection `result` back to the provider as a `tool_result` message, allowing the model to issue a corrected tool call on the next round and complete the turn within `maxToolRounds` ([validated by: returns a schema rejection as a tool_result in the orchestrator loop so the model can correct the call on the next round](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L112)).

## Worked tool example

- The worked weather executor preserves a schema-valid empty `location` string in its result instead of replacing it with a fallback name ([validated by: preserves a schema-valid empty weather location](../../src/orchestration/tools/weather-tool.test.ts#L6)).

- Write prompts as natural user questions, not technical descriptions
- Keep them short and specific -- they appear as pill-shaped buttons in the UI
- 1-2 prompts per tool is enough; the total across all tools should stay manageable
- Use realistic terminology relevant to your application domain

### Defining the input schema

The `inputSchema` follows [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/) format. The model uses this to construct the correct input, and the registry validates it before calling the executor.

- Use `required` to mark mandatory fields
- Add `description` to each property -- the model reads these
- Tool parameter names use `snake_case` (this is the convention from the AI provider API, wrap them in `/* eslint-disable camelcase */` comments)

### Writing the executor

A `ToolExecutor` is an async function that takes the tool input and returns either a string or a `ToolResponse`:

<!-- doc-block: src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts#ToolExecutor -->

```typescript
type ToolExecutor = (input: Record<string, unknown>, context?: ToolContext) => Promise<string | ToolResponse>;
```

The optional `context` provides `userId`, `sessionId`, `workspaceId`, and `authHeaders` for tools that need to make authenticated API calls.

- Return `JSON.stringify(result)` for most tools -- the result gets added to the conversation as a tool result message
- Read known input fields using their schema-declared types; TypeScript may still need an assertion because `ToolExecutor` accepts a generic record
- Handle undeclared extra properties if your tool needs to; they pass through unchanged

Input that fails the schema is returned to the model as a tool result describing the failure. The executor is not called for that input.

For tools that need to send messages directly to the client or suppress the AI's echo, return a `ToolResponse` object instead of a plain string. See [tool-responses.md](../specs/hal-engine-tool-responses/spec.md) for a full walkthrough.

## Step 2: Register the tool

Open `src/orchestration/tools/index.ts` and add two lines:

<!-- doc-block: example/register-tool.ts#register -->

```typescript
- **OpenAI / ChatGPT** (stub with guidance for implementation)
- **Anthropic / Claude** (stub with guidance for implementation)
- **Mock Provider** (built-in for testing)

Providers are abstractly defined via the `AIProvider` interface and instantiated through the `createProvider()` factory. A method that is not implemented throws a descriptive error carrying implementation guidance. Status is per method rather than per provider, and `README.md` carries the only matrix - a second copy would drift.

### 2. Tool System

- Dynamic tool registration via `ToolRegistry`
- JSON Schema tool definitions, declared per tool and forwarded to the model; the registry validates model input against the schema before running the executor and passes schema-valid extra properties through unmodified
- Schema rejection is returned to the model as a tool result, not thrown as an exception; the configured maximum tool rounds (default: 5) bounds correction attempts
- Parallel tool execution within configurable tool loops
- Tool response normalization (supports both simple strings and structured content)
- Context-aware tool execution: the executor receives the caller's identity (`userId`, `sessionId`, `workspaceId`) and the auth headers the session carries, forwarded from the WebSocket upgrade or the HTTP chat request, not the conversation history
- Configurable maximum tool loop iterations (default: 5)

- Maximum tool loop iterations enforce termination (prevents infinite loops)
- Tools execute in response to explicit `ToolCall` objects from the model
- Tool results are returned to the model for incorporation into response
- Tool failures are communicated via `ToolResultMessage` with error content

### 2. Message Ordering

- User messages must precede assistant responses
- Tool results must follow corresponding tool calls
- Thinking entries (when present) appear before tool calls or text
- All entries within a single assistant response are committed atomically
- Session history is immutable after commit

### 3. Authentication & Authorization

- WebSocket connections require successful `WsAuthenticator` callback
- Invalid tokens result in connection rejection
- Each session is bound to exactly one authenticated user
- User context is available to tools and infrastructure components
- The chat routes require an identified user: with no middleware configured, or middleware that attaches no usable `user.id`, they answer `401`

# Changelog

All notable changes to `@re-cinq/hal-engine` are documented here.

The format is [Keep a Changelog 1.1.0](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project adheres to
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html). Entries are written for somebody installing the
package, not for somebody reading this repository's commit log.

## [Unreleased]

### Changed

- Tool registration now rejects an invalid static input schema immediately and names the tool. Tool authors can correct a malformed schema before handling conversations.
- Tool calls with input that fails the declared schema now return a descriptive tool result to the model so it can correct the call. Schema-valid input reaches the executor unchanged, including extra properties.
- In `0.4.0`, executors that used to validate malformed tool input themselves will receive only input accepted by their declared schema once registry validation is enabled. An executor that relied on producing its own error for malformed input will no longer see that input.

## [0.3.0] - 2026-09-17

### Changed

- `HalEngineConfig.orchestrator.hooks` now carries a JSDoc comment. The field already shipped
  in `0.2.x`; the comment makes the lifecycle-hook seam discoverable from the published type
  declarations so editors surface it on hover without a trip to the README.

## [0.2.1] - 2026-09-14

Identical to `0.2.0` — same files, same code. It exists to prove that a release publishes with no
credential stored in the repository: `0.2.0` had to be published with a token, because the registry
cannot hold a trusted publisher for a name that has never been published, and this is the first version
released through that publisher instead. There is nothing here to upgrade for.

scripts/check-spec-links.mjs:5:// of @re-cinq/eslint-plugin-re-lint (AGENTS.md § Spec Test Links).

`.specify/spec.md` is exempt from this section. It is the repo-level system
spec, it predates the convention, and its content is deliberately frozen -
giving it a header table and a lead paragraph would mean writing new prose into
a file that is meant to stay unchanged. The exemption covers the header table
and the lead paragraph only: the Lore coverage job does scan
`.specify/spec.md`, so link placement still applies to it.

## Spec Test Links

Statements in `specs/*/spec.md` cite their validating test in a trailing
parenthetical at the end of the statement, where a list item counts as one
statement and a paragraph counts per sentence. Tests live beside their source
in this repo, so the path points into `src/`:

```markdown
- All entries within a single assistant response are committed before the next
  user message is processed
  ([validated by: commits every entry before the next user message](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L42)).
```

The citation carries the test's **name** as well as its line. The name is what the
author cited; the line is a derived pointer, and it goes stale on its own - adding
an import above a suite moves every test below it, and the citation lands on a
different, still-valid declaration without anything noticing. `npm run spec:names`
holds each citation to the test it names, and `npm run spec:names:fix` repoints the
line from the name. The `#Lnn` stays because the lint rule and the coverage job
both index by it; a citation without one marks the whole file covered rather than
one test.
